clue.text: Bird behind tobacco plant

indicators.note: behind tells us the bird comes after the tobacco in the answer

parts.note: Virginia is a well-known type of tobacco, named after the American state
the creeper is a small bird that climbs tree trunks

explanation.surface: A bird lurks at the back of a tobacco crop.
explanation.definitionFit: A climbing vine grown on walls for its red autumn leaves is a familiar garden plant.

clue.text: Criminal's house and home

parts.note: a villa is a large house
in means at home

explanation.surface: A crook owns both a mansion and a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer, especially a scoundrel in a story, is a criminal.

clue.text: Get bow ready — Robin's had change of heart

indicators.note: a change of heart swaps the middle letter of the name for another

parts.note: the name Robin, with its possessive

explanation.surface: Robin readies a bow after changing their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart of ROBIN is its middle letter B; it becomes S.
explanation.definitionFit: Violinists rub resin on the hair of the bow to prepare it for playing.

clue.text: One elderly relative, one friend — how dull!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
nan is a grandmother
I is the Roman numeral for one
mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A grandmother and a friend make a tedious pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifeless and lacking spirit means dull, a synonym.

clue.text: Bit of verse from William Blake

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the name

explanation.surface: A fragment of poetry by William Blake.
explanation.definitionFit: A metrical foot of one short and one long syllable is a unit of verse.

clue.text: Superficially improving Greek island — alien given some rights by Greeks

parts.note: Cos (Kos) is an island in the Dodecanese

parts.words: alien given some rights by Greeks
parts.note: a metic was a resident foreigner in an ancient Greek city with limited civic rights

explanation.surface: An island visitor is granted some rights by the Greeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatments that only improve the outward look are cosmetic, a synonym.

clue.text: There's talk of a medal for Earl Marshal, for example

indicators.note: talk of points to the spoken form of the letters

parts.note: MC is the Military Cross

explanation.surface: Rumour of a decoration for a senior court official.
explanation.walkthrough: The Earl Marshal organises great state ceremonies, so is a master of ceremonies.
explanation.definitionFit: A master of ceremonies runs formal events, as the Earl Marshal does.

clue.text: Dives as dog runs into another pet

parts.note: Pluto is Mickey Mouse's dog in Disney cartoons

indicators.note: into means the letter goes inside the other pet

parts.note: a cat is another kind of pet
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A dog dives as it chases another pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dives' is not a verb: Dives is the rich man in the parable of Lazarus.
explanation.definitionFit: The rich man of Luke's gospel is a type of the wealthy plutocrat.

clue.text: Sally, soprano caught up in ceremonial

indicators.note: in places the singer's letters within the ceremony

parts.note: a rite is a ceremonial act

indicators.note: in a down clue being caught up means the word is lifted and read upwards

explanation.surface: A girl named Sally, a soprano, is swept up in a ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: Sally is not a girl here but a witty retort; 'sop.' is a dictionary abbreviation for soprano, and in a down clue 'caught up' lifts it to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a quick witty reply, as is a riposte.

clue.text: Girl receives prize — a port

indicators.note: receives means the girl takes the other letters inside her

parts.note: lass is an everyday word for a girl
the palm is a prize or award, as in bearing the palm

explanation.surface: A girl wins a prize and is named as a port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receives' puts PALMA (prize plus A) inside LASS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Canary Islands city is a major Atlantic harbour, so it is a port.

clue.text: Dull report Conservative presented to Parliament once

parts.note: the Rump Parliament sat in England in the 1640s and 1650s

explanation.surface: A Tory reports to the House in a dull, old-fashioned way.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rump was the remnant of the Long Parliament after Pride's Purge of 1648.
explanation.definitionFit: The word imitates the muffled thud of a distant explosion, a dull heavy sound.

clue.text: A loose woman in the family

parts.note: to loose a knot is to untie it

explanation.surface: A woman of loose morals turns out to be a relative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' reads as an adjective describing the woman, but it is the verb meaning set free.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's sister is a female relative, and this is the familiar form of that word.

clue.text: Could our genes make us liberal like this?

indicators.note: asking what the words could make invites rearranging their letters
asking what the words could make invites rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A question about whether our DNA determines open-handedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean lavish or open-handed in giving, a synonym.

clue.text: Girl left as usual

parts.note: Norma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl departed, just as she always does.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are ordinary or standard are just as they usually are.

clue.text: Musical entertainment with a sort of cake and bread

parts.note: a rock cake is a small rough-surfaced bun
'n' is a casual contraction of and
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A show with cake and bread laid on.
explanation.walkthrough: A rock cake is a British teatime bun with a rough, rocky surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1950s popular music style is a form of musical entertainment.

clue.text: Produce conviction — time to regret joining gang

parts.note: a ring is a gang, as in a drugs ring
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Joining a gang leads to a conviction and time to regret it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface wants a criminal conviction; the definition means sounding convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: A statement that sounds genuine carries belief, so it convinces the hearer.

clue.text: Cast preen and preen again, after opening, in here?

indicators.note: after the opening means the letters go after the first letter of the other word

parts.note: to groom is another word for preen

indicators.note: cast means its first letter is thrown off

parts.note: the word preen as written

explanation.surface: Actors preen and preen again before going on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the actors, and they do belong to the definition's picture, but it also throws off the first letter of the first preen; 'after opening' means after the G that begins the synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors relax in the backstage lounge before going on, so the cast are in it.

clue.text: The state of fatherhood that's attained by Asian breadwinner?

definitions.text: The state of fatherhood that's attained by Asian breadwinner?

parts.words: The state of fatherhood that's attained by Asian breadwinner?
parts.note: read as a dad's domain, the state of being a poppa, while an Asian bread wins its place as a crisp disc

explanation.surface: An Asian earner becomes a father.
explanation.walkthrough: Poppa plus -dom (a state, as in kingdom) gives the state of fatherhood; the 'breadwinner' is a kind of Indian bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin crisp fried Indian flatbread, so an Asian bread.

clue.text: Composer bringing back character such as Figaro, initially

parts.note: J.S. Bach is the composer

indicators.note: bringing back means the word for the character is turned backwards

parts.note: a role is a character played on stage

explanation.surface: A composer revives an operatic character like Figaro.
explanation.walkthrough: Figaro is unmarried in The Barber of Seville and weds in the later Marriage of Figaro, so he was single at first.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried man is single, as Figaro was before his marriage.

clue.text: Accompany round clubs, gaining entrance

indicators.note: round means the first phrase goes around the club letter

parts.note: to accompany someone is to be with them
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Someone escorts a group around the clubs to get in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' reads as a way in but is the verb meaning to enchant.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to enchant them, a synonym.

clue.text: Girl one may get out of breath

indicators.note: getting a word out of the letters suggests remaking them in a new order

explanation.surface: A girl might find herself short of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional female name, so it stands for a girl.

clue.text: Dreadful annoyed, this is soothing

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the letters are badly messed up

explanation.surface: Feeling terribly annoyed, someone finds something calming.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkilling or calming medicine is soothing, a synonym.

clue.text: Breathing space given part of orchestra — flute, perhaps

parts.note: the wind is the section of an orchestra playing blown instruments
a flute is one example of a pipe

explanation.surface: An orchestra's wind section gets a pause for breath, flute included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breathing space' suggests a rest; here it is the airway itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the passage that carries air to the lungs, a space for breathing.

clue.text: Article that poses a number of questions

definitions.meaning: a written essay or piece for a journal

definitions.text: that poses a number of questions
definitions.meaning: an examination set out as a list of questions

explanation.definitionFit: An academic essay is an article, and an exam sheet sets questions.

clue.text: Completely fascinated by outskirts of Tokyo

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone is wholly captivated by the edges of Tokyo.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means as a whole, entirely.

clue.text: Approval bestowed on a good animal

parts.note: OK signals approval
PI, short for pious, means good

explanation.surface: A nod of approval is given to a well-behaved creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The African forest mammal related to the giraffe is an animal.

clue.text: Short drive speeds up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: nips means hurries, as in nips out to the shops

explanation.surface: A brief drive gets faster.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief outing in a car is a drive taken for pleasure.

clue.text: Scouts having disappointing time on way back

indicators.note: on the way back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: a poor result is a disappointing one

explanation.surface: Scouts endure a dismal time on their return journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on way back' turns only the word for disappointing, which then follows the letter for time; 'Scouts' is a noun, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of scouts is called a troop, a collective term.

clue.text: Being tactful, I'd comply with a reform

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tactfully agrees to go along with a reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Tact and skill in dealing with people is the noun sense of this word.

clue.text: Home replay, with minor changes, in European section

indicators.note: changes signals that the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A home replay with a few minor alterations is shown in the European section.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minor' reads as small, but its five letters join the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval empire covered a large part of central Europe, a region of that continent.
